title: Predicting Missing Elements Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A library sorts its books, a music scale repeats after eight notes, and a shopkeeper keeps an empty shelf for stock that is still coming. Sorting, repeating and leaving a gap: the periodic table was built on all three ideas. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 3, Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties) we follow how it was built.

You will see why elements need classifying (31 known in 1800, 63 by 1865, 118 today), then test three attempts on the molecule bench: Dobereiner's triads of 1829 (calcium 40, strontium 88, barium 137, and (40 + 137) / 2 = 88.5), Newlands' law of octaves of 1865 (every eighth element like the first, up to calcium), and Mendeleev's periodic law of 1869. Mendeleev put iodine after tellurium because of its properties, left gaps below aluminium and silicon, and described eka-aluminium and eka-silicon before gallium (1875) and germanium (1886) were found. Then a worked triad example, the exam trap about atomic weight, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 26 of our PUC Chemistry series and the start of Chapter 3.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
